text: [See B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1992) 8 CA4th 78, 102, 9 CR2d 894, 910—policy stated defense would be optional with insurer] [3:551 - 3:559] Reserved. 5. [3:560] No Duty to Defend Employer in Civil Suits: The workers' compensation insurer's duty to defend covered claims against the employer (see Ins.C. §§ 11650-11654) is limited to proceedings before the WCAB. A workers' compensation insurer owes no duty to defend a civil court action for damages against the employer. [La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club, Inc. v. Industrial Indem. Co. (1994) 9 C4th 27, 42-43, 36 CR2d 100, 108-109—no duty to defend former employee's suit alleging wrongful termination in violation of public policy] a. [3:561] Rationale: The civil and workers' compensation systems are distinct. Therefore, there is no potential coverage under a workers' compensation policy for damages awardable in a civil action.
